verses.1:1: There was a man in the land of Uz named Job; and that man was sincere and upright, fearing God and departing from evil.
verses.1:2: And to him were born seven sons and three daughters.
verses.1:3: And his possessions were seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels, also five hundred yoke of oxen and five hundred female donkeys, and an exceedingly large household; and that man was great among all those of the east.
verses.1:4: And his sons would go and hold a banquet from house to house, each one on his own day. And sending word, they would invite their three sisters so that they might eat and drink with them.
verses.1:5: And when the days of the banquet had passed in their cycle, Job would send to them and sanctify them; and rising at daybreak, he would offer burnt offerings for each one. For he would say, "Perhaps my sons have sinned and blessed God in their hearts." Thus Job did every day.
verses.1:6: Now one day, when the sons of God had come to stand in the presence of the Lord, Satan too was there among them.
verses.1:7: To him the Lord said, "Where do you come from?" Answering, he said, "I have traveled around the earth and walked throughout it."
verses.1:8: And the Lord said to him, "Have you observed My servant Job, that there is no one like him on the earth, a sincere and upright man, fearing God and departing from evil?"
verses.1:9: Answering Him, Satan said, "Does Job fear God for nothing?
verses.1:10: Have You not fenced around him and his house and all his wealth on every side? You have blessed the works of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
verses.1:11: But stretch out Your hand a little and touch everything that he possesses, and he will certainly bless You to Your face."
verses.1:12: Therefore the Lord said to Satan, "Look, everything that he has is in your hand; only do not stretch out your hand against him." And Satan went out from the presence of the Lord.
verses.1:13: Now on a certain day, while his sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,
verses.1:14: a messenger came to Job, saying, "The oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were grazing beside them;
verses.1:15: and the Sabeans rushed in and carried off everything, and struck down the servants with the sword; and I alone escaped to report to you."
verses.1:16: And while he was still speaking, another came and said, "The fire of God fell from heaven, touched the sheep and the servants, and consumed them; and I alone fled away to report to you."
verses.1:17: And while he too was still speaking, another came and said, "The Chaldeans formed three bands, and raided the camels and carried them off, and also struck down the servants with the sword; and I alone fled to report to you."
verses.1:18: He was still speaking, and look, another entered and said, "While your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their firstborn brother,
verses.1:19: suddenly a violent wind rushed in from the region of the desert and shook the four corners of the house; and collapsing, it crushed your children, and they died; and I alone fled away to report to you."
verses.1:20: Then Job rose and tore his garments; and having shaved his head, he fell to the ground and worshiped,
verses.1:21: and said, "Naked I came out from the womb of my mother, and naked I will return there. The Lord gave, the Lord took away; just as it pleased the Lord, so it has been done. May the name of the Lord be blessed."
verses.1:22: In all these things Job did not sin with his lips, nor did he speak anything foolish against God.
verses.2:1: Now it came about, when on a certain day the sons of God had come and were standing before the Lord, and Satan had also come among them and was standing in His sight,
verses.2:2: that the Lord said to Satan, "Where do you come from?" Answering, he said, "I have traveled around the earth and walked throughout it."
verses.2:3: And the Lord said to Satan, "Have you observed My servant Job, that there is no one like him on the earth, a sincere and upright man, fearing God and departing from evil, and still retaining innocence? Yet you have moved Me against him to afflict him for nothing."
verses.2:4: Answering Him, Satan said, "Skin for skin, and a man will give everything that he has for his life;
verses.2:5: otherwise, put out Your hand and touch his bone and flesh, and then You will see that he will bless You to Your face."
verses.2:6: Therefore the Lord said to Satan, "Look, he is in your hand; yet preserve his life."
verses.2:7: So Satan went out from the presence of the Lord and struck Job with a most severe sore, from the sole of his foot all the way to the crown of his head;
verses.2:8: and he scraped away the discharge with a potsherd, sitting on a dunghill.
verses.2:9: Now his wife said to him, "Do you still remain in your sincerity? Bless God, and die."
verses.2:10: He said to her, "You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things from the hand of God, why should we not receive evil things?" In all these things Job did not sin with his lips.
verses.2:11: Now when the three friends of Job heard of all the evil that had happened to him, they came, each one from his own place: Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. For they had agreed to come together to visit him and console him.
verses.2:12: And when they lifted up their eyes from a distance, they did not recognize him; and crying out, they wept, and having torn their garments, they scattered dust upon their heads toward heaven.
verses.2:13: And they sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights; and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his pain was intense.
verses.3:1: After these things Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,
verses.3:3: "May the day perish on which I was born, and the night in which it was said, 'A man has been conceived.'
verses.3:4: May that day be turned into darkness; may God not seek it from above, and may it not be illuminated with light.
verses.3:5: May darkness and the shadow of death obscure it; may dense gloom seize it, and may it be wrapped in bitterness.
verses.3:6: May a dark whirlwind possess that night; may it not be counted among the days of the year, nor numbered among the months.
verses.3:7: May that night be solitary, and not worthy of praise.
verses.3:8: May those curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse Leviathan.
verses.3:9: May the stars be darkened by its gloom; may it wait for light and not see it, nor the appearing of the rising dawn;
verses.3:10: because it did not shut the doors of the womb that carried me, nor take away evils from my eyes.
verses.3:11: Why did I not die in the womb? Having come out from the womb, why did I not perish at once?
verses.3:12: Why was I received upon knees? Why was I nursed at breasts?
verses.3:13: For now, sleeping, I would be silent, and in my sleep I would rest
verses.3:14: with kings and consuls of the earth, who build desolate places for themselves,
verses.3:15: or with princes who possess gold and fill their houses with silver;
verses.3:16: or like a hidden miscarried child I would not exist, or like those who were conceived and did not see light.
verses.3:17: There the wicked have ceased from turmoil, and there those exhausted in strength have rested.
verses.3:18: And those once bound, together without trouble, have not heard the voice of the taskmaster.
verses.3:19: The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
verses.3:20: Why has light been given to the wretched, and life to those who are in bitterness of soul,
verses.3:21: who wait for death, and it does not come, like those digging for a treasure,
verses.3:22: and who rejoice exceedingly when they have found the grave?
verses.3:23: To a man whose way is hidden, and whom God has surrounded with darkness?
verses.3:24: Before I eat, I sigh; and just like flooding waters, so is my roaring;
verses.3:25: because the fear that I was fearing has come to me, and what I dreaded has happened.
verses.3:26: Did I not hold back? Did I not keep silent? Did I not remain at rest? And indignation came upon me."
verses.4:1: Now Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.4:2: "If we begin to speak to you, perhaps you will take it badly; yet who will be able to hold back a speech once conceived?
verses.4:3: Look, you have taught many, and you have strengthened weary hands;
verses.4:4: your words have steadied those who were staggering, and you have fortified trembling knees.
verses.4:5: But now a scourge has come upon you, and you have grown faint; it has touched you, and you are deeply troubled.
verses.4:6: Where is your fear, your strength, your endurance, and the perfection of your ways?
verses.4:7: Remember, I implore you, what innocent person ever perished? Or when were the upright blotted out?
verses.4:8: Rather, I have seen that those who practice iniquity, and sow sorrows, and harvest them,
verses.4:9: perished when God blew, and were consumed by the breath of His wrath.
verses.4:10: The roar of the lion, and the voice of the lioness, and the teeth of the cubs of lions have been crushed.
verses.4:11: The tiger has perished because it had no prey, and the cubs of the lion have been scattered.
verses.4:12: Moreover, a hidden word was spoken to me, and as though stealthily my ear received the veins of its whisper.
verses.4:13: In the horror of a night vision, when deep sleep usually overtakes people,
verses.4:14: dread gripped me, and trembling, and all my bones were terrified;
verses.4:15: and as a spirit passed by in my presence, the hairs of my flesh bristled.
verses.4:16: Someone stood there whose face I did not recognize, an image before my eyes, and I heard a voice like that of a gentle breeze:
verses.4:17: 'Will a human being be justified in comparison with God? Or will a man be purer than his Maker?
verses.4:18: Look, those who serve Him are not constant, and in His angels He finds perversity;
verses.4:19: how much more will those who inhabit houses of clay, who have an earthly foundation, be consumed as though by a moth?
verses.4:20: From morning until evening they will be cut down; and because no one understands, they will perish forever.
verses.4:21: And those who remain will be taken away from them; they will die, and not in wisdom.'"
verses.5:1: "Call out, then, if there is anyone who will answer you, and turn to one of the holy ones.
verses.5:2: Truly, anger kills a fool, and envy puts a little one to death.
verses.5:3: I myself have seen a fool with a firm root, and at once I cursed his beauty.
verses.5:4: His sons will be far from safety, and they will be crushed in the gate, and there will be no one to rescue them.
verses.5:5: The hungry will eat his harvest, and an armed man will seize even him, and the thirsty will drink his wealth.
verses.5:6: Nothing on earth happens without a cause, and sorrow does not arise from the ground.
verses.5:7: Man is born for toil, and a bird for flight.
verses.5:8: For this reason I myself will plead with the Lord, and I will set forth my utterance to God:
verses.5:9: who performs great and inscrutable things, and marvels without number;
verses.5:10: who gives rain on the face of the earth, and waters everything with waters;
verses.5:11: who places the humble on high, and raises the grieving up in safety;
verses.5:12: who thwarts the designs of the malicious, so that their hands cannot complete what they had begun;
verses.5:13: who catches the wise in their cunning, and thwarts the counsel of the perverse.
verses.5:14: By day they will run into darkness, and as if at night, so they will grope at midday.
verses.5:15: Yet He will save the needy from the sword of their mouth, and the poor from the hand of the violent one.
verses.5:16: And there will be hope for the needy; but iniquity will close its mouth.
verses.5:17: Blessed is the man who is corrected by God; therefore do not reject the reproof of the Lord:
verses.5:18: for He Himself wounds and heals; He strikes, and His hands will make whole.
verses.5:19: In six tribulations He will deliver you, and in the seventh no evil will touch you.
verses.5:20: In famine He will rescue you from death, and in war from the hand of the sword.
verses.5:21: From the whip of the tongue you will be hidden, and you will not fear calamity when it comes.
verses.5:22: In devastation and famine you will laugh, and you will not dread the beasts of the earth.
verses.5:23: But your covenant will be with the stones of the regions, and the beasts of the earth will be at peace with you.
verses.5:24: And you will know that your tent has peace; and inspecting your beauty, you will not sin.
verses.5:25: You will also know that your seed will be manifold, and your descendants like the grass of the earth.
verses.5:26: In abundance you will enter the grave, just as a heap of wheat is carried in during its season.
verses.5:27: See, as we have investigated this, so it is: now that it has been heard, ponder it carefully in your mind."
verses.6:2: "If only my sins by which I have deserved wrath, and the calamity that I endure, were weighed on a scale!
verses.6:3: Like the sand of the sea, this would seem heavier; for this reason my words too are full of pain,
verses.6:4: because the arrows of the Lord are in me, whose indignation drinks up my spirit, and the terrors of the Lord wage war against me.
verses.6:5: Will a wild donkey bray when it has grass? Or will an ox bellow when it stands before a full manger?
verses.6:6: Or can something tasteless be eaten that is not seasoned with salt? Or can anyone taste what, once tasted, brings death?
verses.6:7: The things that my soul previously refused to touch, now, because of distress, are my food.
verses.6:8: Who would grant that my request might come, and that God would give me what I await?
verses.6:9: And that He who began would Himself crush me, release His hand, and cut me off?
verses.6:10: And may this be my consolation, that while afflicting me with pain He would not spare, nor would I contradict the words of the Holy One.
verses.6:11: For what is my strength, that I should endure? Or what is my end, that I should act patiently?
verses.6:12: Neither is my strength the strength of stones, nor is my flesh of bronze.
verses.6:13: Look, there is no help for me in myself, and my close companions too have departed from me.
verses.6:14: The one who takes mercy away from his friend abandons the fear of the Lord.
verses.6:15: My brothers have passed me by, like a torrent that swiftly passes in the valleys.
verses.6:16: Those who fear frost, snow will rush upon them.
verses.6:17: At the time when they are scattered, they will perish; and when it grows hot, they will dissolve from their place.
verses.6:18: The paths of their steps are tangled; they will walk into emptiness and perish.
verses.6:19: Examine the paths of Tema, the routes of Sheba, and wait a little while.
verses.6:20: They were confounded because I hoped; they came right up to me as well, and were covered with shame.
verses.6:21: Now you have come; and now, seeing my wound, you are afraid.
verses.6:22: Did I say, 'Bring to me, and from your possessions give to me'?
verses.6:23: Or, 'Free me from the hand of the enemy, and rescue me from the hand of the strong'?
verses.6:24: Teach me, and I will keep silent; and if by chance I have been ignorant of anything, instruct me.
verses.6:25: Why have you disparaged the words of truth, when there is no one among you who can refute me?
verses.6:26: You compose speeches only to rebuke, and you utter words into the wind.
verses.6:27: You rush upon the orphan, and you strive to overthrow your friend.
verses.6:28: Nevertheless, finish what you have begun; lend an ear, and see whether I am lying.
verses.6:29: Answer, I beg you, without contention; and speaking what is just, judge.
verses.6:30: And you will not find iniquity on my tongue, nor will folly resound in my throat."
verses.7:1: "Warfare is the life of man on the earth, and his days are like the days of a hired worker.
verses.7:2: Just as a slave longs for the shade, and just as a hired worker waits for the end of his work,
verses.7:3: so I too have had empty months, and I have counted out toilsome nights for myself.
verses.7:4: If I sleep, I will say, 'When will I rise?' And again I will wait for the evening, and I will be filled with pains until darkness.
verses.7:5: My flesh is clothed with decay, and with the filth of dust my skin has dried up and contracted.
verses.7:6: My days have passed more swiftly than a web is cut off by a weaver, and they have been consumed without any hope.
verses.7:7: Remember that my life is wind, and my eye will not return to see good things.
verses.7:8: Nor will the sight of man look upon me; Your eyes are on me, and I will not remain.
verses.7:9: Just as a cloud is consumed and passes away, so the one who descends to the underworld will not ascend.
verses.7:10: Nor will he return any more to his house, nor will his place recognize him any longer.
verses.7:11: Therefore I too will not spare my mouth; I will speak in the tribulation of my spirit; I will converse with the bitterness of my soul.
verses.7:12: Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that You have surrounded me with a prison?
verses.7:13: If I say, 'My bed will console me, and I will be relieved talking to myself on my couch,'
verses.7:14: You will terrify me through dreams, and through visions You will shake me with horror.
verses.7:15: For this reason my soul has chosen hanging, and my bones death.
verses.7:16: I have despaired; by no means will I live any longer; spare me, for my days are nothing.
verses.7:17: What is man, that You magnify him? Or why do You set Your heart toward him?
verses.7:18: You visit him at daybreak, and suddenly You test him.
verses.7:19: How long will You not spare me, nor let me go so that I may swallow my saliva?
verses.7:20: I have sinned; what shall I do to You, guardian of men? Why have You placed me contrary to You, and I have become burdensome to my very self?
verses.7:21: Why do You not take away my sin, and why do You not remove my iniquity? Look, now I will sleep in the dust, and if You seek me in the morning, I will not remain."
verses.8:1: Now Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.8:2: "How long will you speak such things, and will the words of your mouth be a manifold wind?
verses.8:3: Does God overthrow judgment, or does the Almighty subvert what is just?
verses.8:4: Even if your children sinned against Him, and He left them in the hand of their own iniquity,
verses.8:5: yet if you rise up at daybreak to God and implore the Almighty;
verses.8:6: if you walk pure and upright, immediately He will awaken for you and make peaceful the dwelling place of your righteousness,
verses.8:7: so much so that if your former things were small, your latter things too will be multiplied exceedingly.
verses.8:8: For inquire of the former generation, and diligently search out the memory of the fathers
verses.8:9: (for indeed we are of yesterday and do not know, because our days upon the earth are like a shadow),
verses.8:10: and they themselves will teach you, speak to you, and from their heart bring forth sayings.
verses.8:11: Can a rush live without moisture, or sedge grow without water?
verses.8:12: While it is still in bloom and is not plucked by hand, it withers before all plants.
verses.8:13: Such are the ways of all who forget God, and the hope of the hypocrite will perish.
verses.8:14: His folly will not please him, and his confidence is like a web of spiders.
verses.8:15: He will lean upon his house, and it will not stand; he will prop it up, and it will not rise.
verses.8:16: He appears moist before the sun comes, and at its rising his shoot will go forth.
verses.8:17: Upon a heap of rocks his roots will grow dense, and among the stones he will dwell.
verses.8:18: If one swallows him up from his place, it will deny him and say, 'I do not know you.'
verses.8:19: For this is the joy of his way, that from the earth others may sprout again.
verses.8:20: God will not cast away the guileless one, nor extend a hand to the wicked,
verses.8:21: until your mouth is filled with laughter, and your lips with jubilation.
verses.8:22: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the tent of the ungodly will not endure."
verses.9:2: "Truly I know that it is so, and that a man is not justified when compared with God.
verses.9:3: If he wishes to contend with Him, he will not be able to answer Him one for a thousand.
verses.9:4: He is wise in heart and strong in might; who has resisted Him and had peace?
verses.9:5: He who moved the mountains, and those whom He overturned in His fury did not know.
verses.9:6: He who shakes the earth from its place, and its pillars are shaken.
verses.9:7: He who commands the sun, and it does not rise, and shuts up the stars as under a seal.
verses.9:8: He who alone stretches out the heavens, and treads upon the waves of the sea.
verses.9:9: He who makes Arcturus and Orion, and the Hyades and the inner regions of the south.
verses.9:10: He who does great and incomprehensible things, and wonders of which there is no number.
verses.9:11: If He comes to me, I will not see Him; if He departs, I will not understand.
verses.9:12: If He suddenly questions, who will answer Him? Or who can say, 'Why do You do so?'
verses.9:13: God, whose wrath no one can resist, and beneath whom those who bear the world bow down.
verses.9:14: How great am I, then, that I should answer Him and speak with Him in my words?
verses.9:15: Even if I have anything just, I will not answer, but I will implore my Judge.
verses.9:16: And when He listens to me as I call, I do not believe that He has heard my voice.
verses.9:17: For in a whirlwind He will crush me, and He will multiply my wounds, even without cause.
verses.9:18: He does not allow my spirit to rest, and He fills me with bitterness.
verses.9:19: If strength is sought, He is the mightiest; if equity of judgment, no one dares to bear witness for me.
verses.9:20: If I wish to justify myself, my mouth will condemn me; if I show myself innocent, it will prove me perverse.
verses.9:21: Even if I am guileless, my soul will not know this very thing, and I will be weary of my life.
verses.9:22: There is one thing that I have spoken: He Himself consumes both the innocent and the ungodly.
verses.9:23: If He scourges, let Him kill once for all, and let Him not laugh at the punishments of the innocent.
verses.9:24: The earth has been given into the hands of the ungodly; He covers the face of its judges. And if it is not He, who then is it?
verses.9:25: My days were swifter than a runner; they fled, and they did not see good.
verses.9:26: They passed by like ships carrying fruit, like an eagle flying to its prey.
verses.9:27: When I say, 'I will by no means speak like this,' I change my countenance, and I am tormented with pain.
verses.9:28: I dreaded all my works, knowing that You would not spare the offender.
verses.9:29: Yet if even so I am ungodly, why have I labored in vain?
verses.9:30: If I wash myself as with waters of snow, and my hands shine as though completely clean,
verses.9:31: yet You will plunge me in filth, and my garments will abhor me.
verses.9:32: For it is not a man who is like me that I will answer, nor one who can be heard with me on equal terms in judgment.
verses.9:33: There is no one who is able to reprove each of the two, and to lay his hand upon both.
verses.9:34: Let Him remove His rod from me, and let His dread not terrify me.
verses.9:35: I will speak, and I will not fear Him; for I cannot answer while afraid."
verses.10:1: "My soul is tired of my life; I will release my speech against myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.10:2: I will say to God, 'Do not condemn me; show me why You judge me in this way.
verses.10:3: Does it seem good to You if You falsely accuse me, and oppress me, the work of Your hands, and assist the counsel of the wicked?
verses.10:4: Do You have eyes of flesh? Or as a man sees, will You also see?
verses.10:5: Are Your days like the days of a man, and are Your years like human times,
verses.10:6: that You should seek my iniquity and examine my sin,
verses.10:7: and know that I have done nothing wicked, when there is no one who can rescue from Your hand?
verses.10:8: Your hands made me and formed me completely all around; and do You cast me down so suddenly?
verses.10:9: Remember, I pray, that You made me like clay, and You will return me to dust.
verses.10:10: Did You not milk me like milk, and curdle me like cheese?
verses.10:11: With skin and flesh You clothed me; with bones and sinews You joined me together.
verses.10:12: Life and mercy You granted me, and Your visitation guarded my spirit.
verses.10:13: Even though You hide these things in Your heart, still I know that You remember all things.
verses.10:14: If I have sinned, and You spared me for an hour, why do You not allow me to be clean from my iniquity?
verses.10:15: And if I am wicked, woe to me; and if righteous, I will not lift my head, sated with affliction and misery.
verses.10:16: And because of pride You will capture me like a lioness, and returning, You torment me astonishingly.
verses.10:17: You renew Your witnesses against me, and multiply Your anger against me, and punishments wage war against me.
verses.10:18: Why did You bring me out of the womb? If only I had been consumed, so that no eye might see me.
verses.10:19: I would have been as though I were not, carried across from the womb to the tomb.
verses.10:20: Will not the small number of my days soon be ended? Leave me alone, therefore, so that I may mourn my pain a little,
verses.10:21: before I go, and do not return, to a land dark and covered with the gloom of death:
verses.10:22: a land of misery and darkness, where the shadow of death is, and no order, but eternal horror dwells.'"
verses.11:1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
verses.11:2: "Will the one who speaks much not also hear? Or will a talkative man be justified?
verses.11:3: Will people stay silent for you alone? And when you have mocked others, will you be refuted by no one?
verses.11:4: For you have said, 'My speech is pure, and I am clean in Your sight.'
verses.11:5: And if only God would speak with you, and open His lips to you,
verses.11:6: so that He might show you the secrets of wisdom, and that His law is manifold; and you would understand that far less is demanded of you by Him than your iniquity deserves!
verses.11:7: Will you perhaps comprehend the footsteps of God, and discover the Almighty even to perfection?
verses.11:8: He is higher than heaven, and what will you do? Deeper than the underworld, and how will you come to know?
verses.11:9: His measure is longer than the earth, and wider than the sea.
verses.11:10: If He overturns all things, or compresses them into one, who will speak against Him?
verses.11:11: For He Himself knows the emptiness of people; and seeing iniquity, does He not consider it?
verses.11:12: An empty man is raised up into pride, and thinks himself born free like the colt of a wild donkey.
verses.11:13: But you have made your heart firm, and have stretched out your hands to Him.
verses.11:14: If you remove from yourself the iniquity that is in your hand, and injustice does not remain in your tent,
verses.11:15: then you will be able to lift your face without blemish; and you will be steadfast, and you will not fear.
verses.11:16: You will also forget misery, and remember it like waters that have passed by.
verses.11:17: And radiance like noonday will rise up for you at evening; and when you think yourself consumed, you will rise like the morning star.
verses.11:18: And you will have confidence, with hope set before you; and buried, you will sleep securely.
verses.11:19: You will rest, and there will be no one to frighten you; and very many will plead before your face.
verses.11:20: But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will perish from them; and their hope is an abomination of the soul."
verses.12:2: "So then, are you the only people, and will wisdom die with you?
verses.12:3: I also have a heart just as you do, nor am I inferior to you; for who is ignorant of these things that you know?
verses.12:4: The one who is mocked by his friend, as I am, will call upon God, and He will hear him; for the simplicity of the righteous man is mocked.
verses.12:5: A lamp held in contempt in the thoughts of the rich is prepared for the appointed time.
verses.12:6: The tents of robbers abound, and they boldly provoke God, although He Himself has given all things into their hands.
verses.12:7: Indeed, question the beasts, and they will teach you; and the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
verses.12:8: Speak to the earth, and it will answer you, and the fish of the sea will recount it.
verses.12:9: Who is unaware that the hand of the Lord has made all these things?
verses.12:10: In His hand is the soul of every living thing, and the spirit of all human flesh.
verses.12:11: Does not the ear judge words, and the palate of the one who eats, flavor?
verses.12:12: In the aged is wisdom, and in much time is prudence.
verses.12:13: With Him are wisdom and strength; He Himself has counsel and understanding.
verses.12:14: If He tears down, there is no one who can build; if He shuts a man in, there is no one who can open.
verses.12:15: If He holds back the waters, all things will dry up; and if He lets them out, they will overturn the earth.
verses.12:16: With Him are strength and wisdom; He Himself knows both the deceiver and the one who is deceived.
verses.12:17: He leads counselors to a foolish end, and judges into stupor.
verses.12:18: He unfastens the belt of kings, and binds their waists with a rope.
verses.12:19: He leads priests without honor, and supplants the nobles:
verses.12:20: changing the lip of the truthful, and taking away the teaching of the elders.
verses.12:21: He pours out contempt upon princes, raising up those who had been oppressed.
verses.12:22: He reveals deep things out of darkness, and brings the shadow of death out into the light.
verses.12:23: He multiplies nations and destroys them, and restores them completely after they have been overturned.
verses.12:24: He changes the heart of the princes of the people of the earth, and deceives them so that they walk in vain through a pathless place:
verses.12:25: they will grope as though in darkness, and not in light, and He will make them wander like drunkards."
verses.13:1: "Look, my eye has seen all these things, and my ear has heard, and I have understood each one.
verses.13:2: In accordance with your knowledge, I too know, and I am not inferior to you.
verses.13:3: Yet still I will speak to the Almighty, and I long to dispute with God,
verses.13:4: first showing you to be fabricators of falsehood and devotees of perverse doctrines.
verses.13:5: And if only you would keep silent, so that you might be considered wise.
verses.13:6: Hear, then, my rebuke, and pay attention to the judgment of my lips.
verses.13:7: Does God really need your falsehood, that you should speak deceptions for Him?
verses.13:8: Do you really show partiality to Him, and strive to judge for God?
verses.13:9: Or will it please Him, from whom nothing can be hidden? Or will He be deceived, like a man, by your frauds?
verses.13:10: He Himself will rebuke you, because in secret you show partiality to Him.
verses.13:11: As soon as He stirs Himself, He will throw you into turmoil, and His terror will rush upon you.
verses.13:12: Your memory will be likened to ashes, and your necks will be reduced to mud.
verses.13:13: Keep silent for a short while, so that I may speak whatever my mind suggests to me.
verses.13:14: Why am I tearing my flesh with my teeth, and carrying my soul in my hands?
verses.13:15: Even if He kills me, in Him I will hope; even so, I will argue my ways in His presence.
verses.13:16: And He Himself will be my savior, for not a single hypocrite will come into His presence.
verses.13:17: Hear my speech, and grasp the riddles with your ears.
verses.13:18: If I am judged, I know that I will be found righteous.
verses.13:19: Who is there who would contend in judgment with me? Let him come. Why am I consumed while keeping silent?
verses.13:20: Just two things do not do to me, and then I will not be hidden from Your face:
verses.13:21: keep Your hand far away from me, and do not let Your dread terrify me.
verses.13:22: Call me, and I will answer You, or at least let me speak, and You answer me.
verses.13:23: How many iniquities and sins do I have? Show me my crimes and offenses.
verses.13:24: Why are You hiding Your face and regarding me as Your enemy?
verses.13:25: Against a leaf that is snatched away by the wind, You display Your power, and You pursue dry stubble:
verses.13:26: for You write bitter things against me, and You wish to consume me by the sins of my youth.
verses.13:27: You have placed my foot in the stocks, and You have watched all my paths, and You have examined the prints of my feet:
verses.13:28: I, who am to be consumed like decay, and like a garment that is eaten by a moth.
verses.14:1: Man, born from a woman, living a brief time, is filled with many woes.
verses.14:2: He emerges like a flower and is crushed, and he flees like a shadow, and never remains in the same condition.
verses.14:3: And do You consider it worthy to open Your eyes upon such a one, and to bring him into judgment with You?
verses.14:4: Who can make clean the one conceived from unclean seed? Is it not You, who alone are?
verses.14:5: Brief are the days of man; the number of his months is with You; You have set his limits, which cannot be crossed.
verses.14:6: Withdraw a little from him, so that he may rest, until his longed-for day comes, like that of a hired worker.
verses.14:7: A tree has hope: if it is cut down, it grows green again, and its branches sprout.
verses.14:8: If its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies away in the dust,
verses.14:9: at the scent of water it will bud, and produce foliage just as when it was first planted.
verses.14:10: But when a man dies, and is stripped bare and consumed, where, I ask, is he?
verses.14:11: Just as if waters were to recede from the sea, and a river, emptied out, were to dry up:
verses.14:12: so a man, when he has fallen asleep, will not rise again; until heaven is worn away, he will not wake up, nor will he rise up from his sleep.
verses.14:13: Who would grant me this, that You would protect me in the underworld, and hide me until Your fury passes by, and set a time for me in which You would remember me?
verses.14:14: Do You suppose that a dead man will live again? All the days in which I now serve as a soldier, I am waiting until my change comes.
verses.14:15: You will call me, and I will answer You; to the work of Your hands You will extend Your right hand.
verses.14:16: You have indeed counted my steps, yet spare my sins.
verses.14:17: You have sealed my offenses as though in a pouch, yet You have healed my iniquity.
verses.14:18: A falling mountain slips away, and a rock is shifted from its place:
verses.14:19: waters hollow out stones, and by flooding the earth is gradually consumed; and therefore You will likewise destroy man.
verses.14:20: You made him strong for a little while, so that he would pass away forever; You will alter his face and send him away.
verses.14:21: Whether his sons are noble or ignoble, he will not understand.
verses.14:22: Yet still, his flesh, while he lives, will feel pain, and his soul will mourn over himself."
verses.15:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.15:2: "Will a wise man reply like one speaking into the wind, and fill his stomach with scorching heat?
verses.15:3: You reprove with words one who is not equal to you, and you speak what does not profit you.
verses.15:4: As far as lies in you, you have nullified fear and taken away prayers before God.
verses.15:5: For your iniquity has instructed your mouth, and you imitate the tongue of those who blaspheme.
verses.15:6: Your mouth will condemn you, and not I; and your lips will answer you.
verses.15:7: Were you born as the first man, and formed before the hills?
verses.15:8: Did you hear the counsel of God, and will His wisdom be inferior to you?
verses.15:9: What do you know of which we are ignorant? What do you understand that we do not know?
verses.15:10: Both old men and aged men are among us, much older than your fathers.
verses.15:11: Is it a great thing that God should comfort you? But your perverse words prevent this.
verses.15:12: Why does your heart lift you up, and why, as though contemplating great things, do you have astonished eyes?
verses.15:13: Why does your spirit swell against God, so that you bring forth speeches of this kind from your mouth?
verses.15:14: What is man, that he should be spotless, and that one born of a woman should appear righteous?
verses.15:15: Look, among His holy ones no one is unchangeable, and the heavens are not clean in His sight.
verses.15:16: How much more abominable and useless is man, who drinks iniquity like water?
verses.15:17: I will show you; listen to me; what I have seen I will recount to you.
verses.15:18: Wise men acknowledge and do not conceal their fathers,
verses.15:19: to whom alone the land was given, and no foreigner passed through them.
verses.15:20: All his days the ungodly man is arrogant, and the number of the years of his tyranny is uncertain.
verses.15:21: The sound of terror is always in his ears; and when there is peace, he always suspects an ambush.
verses.15:22: He does not believe that he can return from darkness to light, looking around on all sides for the sword.
verses.15:23: When he moves to seek bread, he knows that a day of darkness is prepared in his hand.
verses.15:24: Tribulation will terrify him, and anguish will besiege him, like a king who is made ready for battle.
verses.15:25: For he has stretched out his hand against God, and has made himself strong against the Almighty.
verses.15:26: He has run against Him with neck held erect, and has armed himself with a fat neck.
verses.15:27: Fatness has covered his face, and fat hangs down from his flanks.
verses.15:28: He has lived in desolate cities, and in deserted houses that have been reduced to mounds.
verses.15:29: He will not become rich, nor will his wealth endure, nor will he send his root into the earth.
verses.15:30: He will not depart from darkness; a flame will wither his branches, and he will be carried away by the breath of his own mouth.
verses.15:31: He will not believe, deceived in vain by error, that he is to be redeemed at any price.
verses.15:32: Before his days are fulfilled, he will perish, and his hands will wither.
verses.15:33: His cluster of grapes will be harmed like a vine in its first blossom, and like an olive tree casting off its blossom.
verses.15:34: For the assembly of the hypocrite is barren, and fire will devour the tents of those who gladly accept bribes.
verses.15:35: He has conceived pain, and has given birth to iniquity, and his womb prepares deceptions."
verses.16:2: "I have frequently heard such things; all of you are burdensome comforters.
verses.16:3: Will windy words have an end? Or is anything troublesome to you if you speak?
verses.16:4: I also could speak things like yours, and if only your soul were in place of my soul:
verses.16:5: I would strengthen you with my mouth, and I would move my lips as though sparing you.
verses.16:6: But what am I to do? If I speak, my pain will not grow quiet, and if I remain silent, it will not depart from me.
verses.16:7: But now my pain has crushed me, and all my limbs have been reduced to nothing.
verses.16:8: My wrinkles give testimony against me, and a liar is raised up against my face, contradicting me.
verses.16:9: He has gathered his fury against me, and threatening me, he has gnashed his teeth against me; my enemy has stared at me with terrible eyes.
verses.16:10: They have opened their mouths against me, and taunting me, they have struck my cheek; they are sated with my torments.
verses.16:11: God has confined me with the unrighteous man, and has given me over into the hands of the ungodly.
verses.16:12: I, the one once wealthy, was suddenly crushed; He seized my neck, shattered me, and set me up for Himself as a target.
verses.16:13: He surrounded me with His spears; He severely wounded my loins; He did not spare, and He poured out my entrails on the ground.
verses.16:14: He slashed me with wound upon wound; He rushed against me like a giant.
verses.16:15: I have stitched sackcloth over my skin, and covered my flesh with ashes.
verses.16:16: My face has swollen from weeping, and my eyelids have grown dim.
verses.16:17: I have suffered these things without iniquity in my hand, while I had pure prayers to God.
verses.16:18: Earth, do not cover my blood, nor let my cry find a place of hiding in you;
verses.16:19: for look, my witness is in heaven, and He who knows me is on high.
verses.16:20: My friends are full of words; my eye streams toward God,
verses.16:21: and if only a man were judged with God just as a son of man is judged with his fellow.
verses.16:22: For look, the brief years pass by, and I walk a path along which I will not return.
verses.17:1: My spirit will be weakened; my days will be cut short, and only the tomb remains for me.
verses.17:2: I have not sinned, and my eye lingers in bitterness.
verses.17:3: Free me, Lord, and place me beside You, and let anyone's hand fight against me.
verses.17:4: You have removed their heart far from discipline; for that reason they will not be exalted.
verses.17:5: He promises plunder to his companions, and the eyes of his children will fail.
verses.17:6: He has set me as a proverb of the common people, and I am an example before them.
verses.17:7: My eye has grown dim from indignation, and my limbs have been reduced as if to nothing.
verses.17:8: The righteous will be astonished at this, and the innocent will be roused against the hypocrite.
verses.17:9: And the righteous man will hold to his way, and to clean hands he will add strength.
verses.17:10: Therefore turn back, all of you, and come, and I will not find any wise man among you.
verses.17:11: My days have gone by; my thoughts have been dispersed, tormenting my heart.
verses.17:12: They have turned night into day, and once again after darkness I hope for light.
verses.17:13: If I wait, the underworld is my house, and in darkness I have spread my bed.
verses.17:14: To decay I have said, 'You are my father'; to worms, 'My mother and my sister.'
verses.17:15: Where then is my expectation now? And who regards my patience?
verses.17:16: All that is mine will descend into the deepest underworld: do you suppose that at least there I will have rest?"
verses.18:1: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.18:2: "How long will you fling out words? Understand first, and thus let us speak.
verses.18:3: Why have we been counted as beasts and become vile before you?
verses.18:4: You who destroy your soul in your fury, will the earth be abandoned because of you, and will the cliffs be moved from their place?
verses.18:5: Will not the light of the ungodly be extinguished, nor will the flame of his fire shine?
verses.18:6: The light will grow dark in his tent, and the lamp that is above him will be extinguished.
verses.18:7: The strides of his strength will be hemmed in, and his own counsel will throw him down.
verses.18:8: For he has thrust his feet into a net, and he walks in its meshes.
verses.18:9: The sole of his foot will be caught in a snare, and thirst will blaze up against him.
verses.18:10: A noose for him is hidden in the ground, and a trap for him on the path.
verses.18:11: On every side terrors will frighten him, and they will entangle his feet.
verses.18:12: May his strength be weakened by hunger, and may starvation assail his ribs.
verses.18:13: May it devour the beauty of his skin; may firstborn death consume his arms.
verses.18:14: May his confidence be torn from his tent, and may destruction trample over him like a king.
verses.18:15: May the companions of the one who is not dwell in his tent; may sulfur be scattered in his tent.
verses.18:16: Below, may his roots be dried up; and above, may his harvest be crushed.
verses.18:17: May his memory perish from the earth, and may his name not be celebrated in the streets.
verses.18:18: He will expel him from light into darkness and remove him from the world.
verses.18:19: There will be no seed of his, nor progeny among his people, nor any remnants in his regions.
verses.18:20: At his day the last will be astonished, and horror will assail the first.
verses.18:21: These therefore are the tents of the unrighteous, and this is the place of the one who does not know God."
verses.19:2: "How long do you afflict my soul and crush me with words?
verses.19:3: Look, ten times you humiliate me, and you are not ashamed while oppressing me.
verses.19:4: Indeed, even if I was ignorant, my ignorance will be with me.
verses.19:5: But you lift yourselves up against me and reprove me with my disgraces.
verses.19:6: At least now understand that God has afflicted me with no fair judgment and has surrounded me with His scourges.
verses.19:7: Look, I will call out, enduring violence, and no one will hear; I will shout aloud, and there is no one who judges.
verses.19:8: He has fenced in my path, and I cannot pass through; and on my footpath He has placed darkness.
verses.19:9: He has stripped me of my glory and removed the crown from my head.
verses.19:10: He has torn me down on every side, and I am perishing; and as from an uprooted tree He has removed my hope.
verses.19:11: His fury has raged against me, and thus He has regarded me as His enemy.
verses.19:12: His raiders have come together and made a way for themselves through me, and they have besieged my tent all around.
verses.19:13: He has removed my brothers far from me, and my acquaintances have withdrawn from me like strangers.
verses.19:14: My relatives have abandoned me, and those who knew me have forgotten me.
verses.19:15: The lodgers of my house and my maidservants have regarded me as a stranger, and I have been like a foreigner in their eyes.
verses.19:16: I called my servant, and he did not answer; with my own mouth I kept imploring him.
verses.19:17: My wife has shuddered at my breath, and I kept pleading with the children of my womb.
verses.19:18: Fools also despised me; and when I had withdrawn from them, they spoke ill of me.
verses.19:19: Those who were formerly my counselors have detested me, and the one whom I loved most has turned away from me.
verses.19:20: With my flesh consumed, my bone has clung to my skin, and only the lips have been left around my teeth.
verses.19:21: Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, at least you, my friends, for the hand of the Lord has touched me.
verses.19:22: Why do you pursue me as God does and satisfy yourselves with my flesh?
verses.19:23: Who would grant me that my words be written? Who would give me that they be inscribed in a book
verses.19:24: with an iron stylus and a plate of lead, or be carved with a chisel in flint?
verses.19:25: For I know that my Redeemer lives, and on the last day I will rise from the earth;
verses.19:26: and once more I will be encompassed with my skin, and in my flesh I will see my God,
verses.19:27: whom I myself will see, and my eyes will gaze upon, and not another: this hope of mine has been stored up in my breast.
verses.19:28: Why then do you now say, 'Let us pursue him, and let us find the root of the matter against him'?
verses.19:29: Flee therefore from the face of the sword, since the sword is the avenger of iniquities; and know that there is a judgment."
verses.20:1: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered and said:
verses.20:2: "For this reason my varied thoughts follow one another, and my mind is swept away in different directions.
verses.20:3: I will hear the instruction by which you reprove me, and the spirit of my understanding will respond to me.
verses.20:4: I know this from the beginning, ever since man was placed upon the earth,
verses.20:5: that the praise of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the hypocrite is like a moment.
verses.20:6: If his pride ascends up to heaven, and his head touches the clouds,
verses.20:7: he will be destroyed like a dung heap in the end, and those who had seen him will say, 'Where is he?'
verses.20:8: Like a dream flying away, he will not be found; he will pass away like a vision of the night.
verses.20:9: The eye that had seen him will not see him, nor will his place look upon him any longer.
verses.20:10: His sons will be worn down by poverty, and his hands will repay him his pain.
verses.20:11: His bones will be filled with the vices of his youth, and they will sleep with him in the dust.
verses.20:12: For when evil is sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.
verses.20:13: He will spare it and will not abandon it, and he will conceal it in his throat.
verses.20:14: His bread in his stomach will be turned into the gall of asps within.
verses.20:15: He will vomit up the riches that he devoured, and God will draw them out of his belly.
verses.20:16: He will suck the head of asps, and the tongue of a viper will kill him.
verses.20:17: (May he not see the streams of the river, the torrents of honey and butter.)
verses.20:18: He will pay for all that he has done, and yet he will not be consumed; according to the multitude of his devices, so also he will suffer.
verses.20:19: For he crushed and stripped the poor; he seized a house and did not build it.
verses.20:20: Nor was his belly satisfied; and when he has the things he had coveted, he will not be able to possess them.
verses.20:21: Nothing was left of his food, and therefore nothing will remain of his goods.
verses.20:22: When he has been satisfied, he will be hemmed in; he will burn, and every pain will rush upon him.
verses.20:23: Oh, that his belly may be filled, so that He may send forth upon him the anger of His wrath, and rain His war upon him.
verses.20:24: He will flee from iron weapons, and he will rush into a bronze bow.
verses.20:25: Drawn out and emerging from its sheath, and flashing in its bitterness: terrifying ones will go and come upon him.
verses.20:26: All darkness is hidden in his secret places; a fire that is not kindled will devour him; the one left in his tent will be afflicted.
verses.20:27: The heavens will uncover his iniquity, and the earth will rise against him.
verses.20:28: The offspring of his house will be laid open; it will be pulled down on the day of the wrath of God.
verses.20:29: This is the share of a wicked man from God, and the inheritance of his words from the Lord."
verses.21:2: "Hear my words, I beg you, and repent.
verses.21:3: Bear with me, and I will speak; and after my words, if it seems good, laugh.
verses.21:4: Is my dispute against a man, so that I should not rightly be grieved?
verses.21:5: Look at me and be astounded, and place a finger over your mouth.
verses.21:6: Even I, when I remember, am terrified, and trembling shakes my flesh.
verses.21:7: Why then do the wicked live, and why have they been lifted up and strengthened with riches?
verses.21:8: Their seed remains before them, a crowd of relatives and grandchildren in their sight.
verses.21:9: Their houses are safe and peaceful, and the rod of God is not on them.
verses.21:10: Their cow has conceived and has not miscarried; the cow has given birth and has not been deprived of her young.
verses.21:11: Their little ones go out like flocks, and their children exult in play.
verses.21:12: They hold the tambourine and the lyre, and they rejoice at the sound of the pipe.
verses.21:13: They spend their days in prosperity, and in a moment they descend to the underworld.
verses.21:14: And they said to God, 'Depart from us, and we do not want the knowledge of Your ways.
verses.21:15: Who is the Almighty, so that we should serve Him? And what benefit is it to us if we pray to Him?'
verses.21:16: Nevertheless, because their good things are not in their hand, may the counsel of the wicked be far from me.
verses.21:17: How often will the lamp of the wicked be extinguished, and will a flood come upon them, and will He apportion the pains of His wrath?
verses.21:18: They will be like chaff before the face of the wind, and like ash that a whirlwind scatters.
verses.21:19: God will reserve for his sons the pain of their father, and when He repays, then he will know.
verses.21:20: His eyes will see his own slaughter, and he will drink from the wrath of the Almighty.
verses.21:21: For what does it matter to him about his house after him, even if the number of his months is cut in half?
verses.21:22: Will anyone teach knowledge to God, who judges those on high?
verses.21:23: This one dies strong and healthy, rich and happy;
verses.21:24: his inward parts are full of fat, and his bones are moistened with marrow;
verses.21:25: but another dies in bitterness of soul, without any wealth;
verses.21:26: and yet together in the dust they will sleep, and worms will cover them.
verses.21:27: Surely I know your thoughts and unjust judgments against me.
verses.21:28: For you say, 'Where is the house of the prince? And where are the tents of the wicked?'
verses.21:29: Ask any of the travelers, and you will recognize that he understands these same things:
verses.21:30: that the evil man is reserved for the day of destruction, and will be led to the day of wrath.
verses.21:31: Who will reprove his way before him? And who will repay him for what he has done?
verses.21:32: He himself will be led to the tombs, and in the heap of the dead he will keep watch.
verses.21:33: He was sweet to the gravel of Cocytus, and he will draw every man after him, and before him countless ones.
verses.21:34: How then do you console me in vain, when your response has been shown to oppose the truth?"
verses.22:1: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said:
verses.22:2: "Can a man be compared to God, even when he possesses perfect knowledge?
verses.22:3: What does it profit God if you are righteous? Or what do you bring to Him if your way is spotless?
verses.22:4: Is it because He is afraid that He will reprove you and come into judgment with you,
verses.22:5: and not because of your very great wickedness and your endless iniquities?
verses.22:6: For you took away the pledge of your brothers without cause, and stripped the naked of their garments.
verses.22:7: You did not give water to the weary, and from the hungry you withheld bread.
verses.22:8: By the strength of your arm you possessed the land, and as the most powerful you held it.
verses.22:9: You sent widows away empty-handed, and you crushed the arms of orphans.
verses.22:10: Therefore you are surrounded by snares, and sudden terror dismays you.
verses.22:11: And did you think that you would not see darkness, and that you would not be overwhelmed by the rush of flooding waters?
verses.22:12: Or do you not consider that God is higher than heaven, and is exalted above the summit of the stars?
verses.22:13: And you say, 'What indeed does God know? And He judges as if through thick darkness.
verses.22:14: Clouds are His hiding place, and He does not consider our affairs, and He walks around the poles of heaven.'
verses.22:15: Do you long to keep the path of the ages, which wicked men have trodden,
verses.22:16: who were carried off before their time, and a river overturned their foundation?
verses.22:17: They kept saying to God, 'Depart from us!' and they regarded Him as though the Almighty could do nothing,
verses.22:18: even though He had filled their houses with good things; may their opinion be far from me.
verses.22:19: The righteous will see and rejoice, and the innocent will mock them:
verses.22:20: 'Has not their elevation been cut down? And has not fire devoured their remnants?'
verses.22:21: Yield to Him, therefore, and have peace, and through these things you will have the finest fruits.
verses.22:22: Receive the law from His mouth, and place His words in your heart.
verses.22:23: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up, and you will remove iniquity far from your tent.
verses.22:24: He will give flint in place of earth, and in place of flint, golden torrents.
verses.22:25: And the Almighty will be against your enemies, and silver will be piled up for you.
verses.22:26: Then you will overflow with delights in the Almighty, and you will lift up your face to God.
verses.22:27: You will pray to Him, and He will heed you, and you will fulfill your vows.
verses.22:28: You will decide a matter, and it will come to you, and light will shine upon your ways.
verses.22:29: For the one who has been humbled will be in glory, and the one who lowers his eyes will himself be saved.
verses.22:30: The innocent will be saved; indeed, he will be saved through the cleanness of his hands."
verses.23:2: "Even now my speech is in bitterness, and the hand of my affliction is heavier than my groaning.
verses.23:3: Who would grant me to know and find Him, and to come all the way to His throne?
verses.23:4: I will lay a case before Him, and I will fill my mouth with reproaches,
verses.23:5: so that I may know the words He answers me, and understand what He speaks to me.
verses.23:6: I do not want Him to contend with me in great strength, nor to press me down with the weight of His greatness.
verses.23:7: Let Him set forth fairness against me, and let my case reach victory.
verses.23:8: If I go to the east, He does not appear; if to the west, I will not perceive Him.
verses.23:9: If to the left, what am I to do? I will not lay hold of Him; if I turn to the right, I will not see Him.
verses.23:10: Yet He Himself knows my way, and He has tested me like gold that passes through fire.
verses.23:11: My foot has followed His footsteps; His way I have kept, and I have not turned aside from it.
verses.23:12: From the commands of His lips I have not departed, and in my bosom I have hidden the words of His mouth.
verses.23:13: For He Himself is alone, and no one can turn aside His thought; and whatever His soul has willed, that He has done.
verses.23:15: And for that reason I am troubled before His face, and as I consider Him, I am disquieted with fear.
verses.23:16: God has made my heart weak, and the Almighty has thrown me into turmoil.
verses.23:17: For I have not perished because of the looming darkness, nor has thick darkness covered my face.
verses.24:1: Times are not hidden from the Almighty, yet those who know Him do not know His days.
verses.24:2: Some have moved boundary markers; they have plundered flocks and pastured them.
verses.24:3: They have driven away the donkey of orphans, and they have taken away the ox of a widow as a pledge.
verses.24:4: They have overturned the way of the poor, and they have oppressed the meek of the earth together.
verses.24:5: Others, like wild donkeys in the desert, go out to their work; watching for prey, they prepare bread for their children.
verses.24:6: They reap a field not their own, and they harvest the vineyard of the one whom they have oppressed by force.
verses.24:7: Taking away their garments, they send men away naked who have no covering in the cold;
verses.24:8: the rains of the mountains drench them, and having no shelter, they embrace the stones.
verses.24:9: They have done violence, plundering orphans, and they have stripped the poor populace.
verses.24:10: From the naked and those who go about without clothing, and from the hungry, they have taken away the heads of grain.
verses.24:11: Among their heaps they have rested at midday, those who, having trodden the winepresses, go thirsty.
verses.24:12: From the cities they have made men groan, and the soul of the wounded has cried out; and God does not allow it to go unavenged.
verses.24:13: They themselves have been rebels against the light; they have not known its ways, nor have they returned along its paths.
verses.24:14: Early in the morning the murderer rises; he kills the needy and the poor, but through the night he will be like a thief.
verses.24:15: The eye of the adulterer watches for thick darkness, saying, 'No eye will see me,' and he will cover his face.
verses.24:16: In darkness he digs through houses, just as they had agreed among themselves by day, and they have not known the light.
verses.24:17: If the dawn suddenly appears, they regard it as the shadow of death, and thus they walk in darkness as though in light.
verses.24:18: He is swift upon the face of the water; may his portion on the earth be cursed, and let him not walk along the way of the vineyards.
verses.24:19: Let him pass from the snow waters to excessive heat, and his sin all the way to the underworld.
verses.24:20: Let mercy forget him; his sweetness is worms; let him not be in remembrance, but let him be crushed like an unfruitful tree.
verses.24:21: For he has fed the barren woman who does not give birth, and to the widow he has done no good.
verses.24:22: He has dragged down the strong in his strength, and when he stands, he will not trust his own life.
verses.24:23: God has given him a place for repentance, and he abuses it for pride; yet His eyes are upon his ways.
verses.24:24: They have been lifted up for a little while, and they will not endure; and they will be humbled like all things, and will be taken away, and like the tops of heads of grain they will be crushed.
verses.24:25: And if it is not so, who can convict me of having lied, and set my words before God?"
verses.25:1: Now Bildad the Shuhite answered and said:
verses.25:2: "Dominion and terror are with Him, who makes harmony in His heights.
verses.25:3: Is there any number to His soldiers? And upon whom will His light not rise?
verses.25:4: Can a man be justified when compared with God? Or can one born of a woman appear clean?
verses.25:5: Look, even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not clean in His sight:
verses.25:6: how much less man, who is decay, and the son of man, who is a worm?"
verses.26:2: "Whose helper are you? Is it of one who is feeble? And do you support the arm of him who is not strong?
verses.26:3: To whom have you given counsel? Perhaps to one who has no wisdom; and you have displayed your abundant understanding.
verses.26:4: Whom did you wish to teach? Was it not Him who made breath?
verses.26:5: Look, the giants groan beneath the waters, and those who live with them.
verses.26:6: The underworld is naked before Him, and destruction has no covering.
verses.26:7: He stretches out the north over emptiness, and suspends the earth over nothing.
verses.26:8: He binds the waters in His clouds, so that they do not burst forth downward together.
verses.26:9: He holds the face of His throne, and spreads out His mist over it.
verses.26:10: He has placed a boundary around the waters, until light and darkness come to an end.
verses.26:11: The pillars of heaven quake and are terrified at His nod.
verses.26:12: By His strength the seas were suddenly gathered together, and His understanding struck the proud one.
verses.26:13: His Spirit adorned the heavens, and with His hand acting as midwife, the twisting serpent was brought forth.
verses.26:14: Look, these things have been spoken in part about His ways; and since we have barely heard a small drop of His word, who will be able to gaze upon the thunder of His greatness?"
verses.27:1: Job also continued, taking up his parable, and said:
verses.27:2: "As God lives, who has taken away my justice, and the Almighty, who has led my soul to bitterness:
verses.27:3: surely, as long as breath remains in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
verses.27:4: my lips will not speak iniquity, nor will my tongue meditate falsehood.
verses.27:5: Far be it from me to judge you to be righteous; until I expire, I will not withdraw from my innocence.
verses.27:6: My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not abandon; for my heart does not reproach me in all my life.
verses.27:7: May my enemy be like an ungodly man, and my adversary like an unjust man.
verses.27:8: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, if he seizes greedily and God does not deliver his soul?
verses.27:9: Will God really hear his outcry when anguish comes upon him?
verses.27:10: Or will he be able to delight in the Almighty and invoke God at all times?
verses.27:11: I will teach you through the hand of God the things that the Almighty has, and I will not hide them.
verses.27:12: Look, all of you know this; and why do you speak empty things without cause?
verses.27:13: This is the portion of an ungodly man with God, and the inheritance of the violent, which they will receive from the Almighty.
verses.27:14: If his sons are multiplied, they will be under the sword, and his descendants will not be satisfied with bread;
verses.27:15: those who remain from him will be buried in ruin, and his widows will not weep.
verses.27:16: If he piles up silver like earth and prepares garments like clay,
verses.27:17: he will indeed prepare them, but the righteous will be clothed in them, and the innocent will divide the silver.
verses.27:18: He has built his house like a moth, and like a watchman he has made a booth.
verses.27:19: The rich man, when he sleeps, will carry nothing away with him; he will open his eyes and find nothing.
verses.27:20: Poverty will seize him like water; at night a storm will overwhelm him.
verses.27:21: A scorching wind will lift him up and carry him off, and like a whirlwind it will tear him from his place.
verses.27:22: And it will hurl upon him and will not spare; fleeing, he will flee from its hand.
verses.27:23: It will clasp its hands over him and hiss at him, gazing upon his place.
verses.28:1: Silver has the sources of its veins, and for gold there is a place in which it is smelted.
verses.28:2: Iron is taken up from the earth, and stone dissolved by heat is turned into copper.
verses.28:3: He has set a time for darkness, and he himself examines the end of all things: the stone of gloom also, and the shadow of death.
verses.28:4: A torrent separates from the traveling people those whom the foot of a needy man has forgotten, and who are inaccessible.
verses.28:5: The earth from which bread sprang forth has been overturned in its place by fire.
verses.28:6: Its stones are the place of sapphire, and its clods are gold.
verses.28:7: No bird has known the path, nor has the eye of the vulture gazed upon it.
verses.28:8: The sons of traders have not trodden it, nor has the lioness passed through it.
verses.28:9: He has stretched out his hand to the flint; he has overturned mountains from the roots.
verses.28:10: In the rocks he has cut out channels, and his eye has seen everything precious.
verses.28:11: He has searched the depths of the rivers also, and has brought hidden things out into the light.
verses.28:12: But where is wisdom found? And what is the place of understanding?
verses.28:13: Man does not know its price, nor is it found in the land of those who live pleasantly.
verses.28:14: The abyss says, 'It is not in me,' and the sea speaks, 'It is not with me.'
verses.28:15: Fine gold will not be given for it, nor will silver be weighed out in exchange for it.
verses.28:16: It will not be compared to the dyed colors of India, nor to the most precious sardonyx stone or sapphire.
verses.28:17: Gold or glass will not be equal to it, nor will vessels of gold be exchanged for it.
verses.28:18: Lofty and prominent things will not be spoken of in comparison with it; yet wisdom is drawn from hidden places.
verses.28:19: The topaz from Ethiopia will not be equal to it, nor will it be matched with the purest dye.
verses.28:20: From where, then, does wisdom come? And what is the place of understanding?
verses.28:21: It is hidden from the eyes of all who live; it also lies concealed from the birds of the sky.
verses.28:22: Destruction and death have said, 'With our ears we have heard its report.'
verses.28:23: God understands its way, and He Himself knows its place.
verses.28:24: For He Himself gazes upon the ends of the world, and observes all things that are under heaven.
verses.28:25: He made a weight for the winds, and weighed out the waters by measure.
verses.28:26: When He was setting a law for the rains, and a way for the resounding storms,
verses.28:27: then He saw it and recounted it, and prepared it, and searched it out.
verses.28:28: And He said to man, 'Look, the fear of the Lord, that itself is wisdom; and to withdraw from evil is understanding.'"
verses.29:1: Job also continued, taking up his parable, and said:
verses.29:2: "Who would grant to me that I might be as in former months, according to the days in which God guarded me,
verses.29:3: when His lamp shone above my head, and by His light I walked in darkness,
verses.29:4: just as I was in the days of my youth, when God was privately in my tent,
verses.29:5: when the Almighty was with me, and my children were all around me,
verses.29:6: when I washed my feet in butter, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me,
verses.29:7: when I went out to the gate of the city, and in the public square they prepared a chair for me?
verses.29:8: The young men saw me and hid themselves, and the old men, rising up, stood.
verses.29:9: Princes stopped speaking and laid a finger over their mouths.
verses.29:10: Leaders held back their voice, and their tongue clung to their throat.
verses.29:11: The hearing ear called me blessed, and the seeing eye gave testimony for me,
verses.29:12: because I had rescued the poor man crying aloud, and the orphan for whom there was no helper.
verses.29:13: The blessing of the one about to perish came upon me, and I consoled the heart of the widow.
verses.29:14: I was clothed with righteousness, and I dressed myself with my judgment as with a garment and a diadem.
verses.29:15: I was an eye for the blind man, and a foot for the lame man.
verses.29:16: I was a father of the poor, and I most diligently searched out the case that I did not know.
verses.29:17: I crushed the jaws of the unjust man, and I carried off the prey from his teeth.
verses.29:18: And I used to say, 'In my little nest I will die, and like a palm tree I will multiply days.
verses.29:19: My root is open beside the waters, and the dew will linger on my harvest.
verses.29:20: My glory will continually be renewed, and my bow will be restored in my hand.'
verses.29:21: Those who listened to me awaited a verdict, and attentively kept silent for my counsel.
verses.29:22: They dared to add nothing to my words, and my speech distilled upon them.
verses.29:23: They awaited me like rain, and they opened their mouths as for the late shower.
verses.29:24: Whenever I smiled at them, they did not believe it, and the light of my face did not fall to the ground.
verses.29:25: If I had wished to go to them, I sat first; and while I sat like a king, with an army standing around, I was nevertheless a comforter of those who mourned.
verses.30:1: But now those younger in age mock me, whose fathers I did not deign to place with the dogs of my flock,
verses.30:2: the strength of whose hands was as nothing to me, and they were considered unworthy of life itself,
verses.30:3: barren from want and hunger, who gnawed in the wilderness, squalid with calamity and misery.
verses.30:4: And they chewed herbs and the bark of trees, and the root of junipers was their food;
verses.30:5: snatching these things from the valleys, whenever they found individual ones, they ran to them with shouting.
verses.30:6: They lived in the desolate places of the torrents, and in the caverns of the earth, or upon the gravel;
verses.30:7: they rejoiced among such things, and counted it a delight to be under the briers,
verses.30:8: sons of fools and of the ignoble, and not visible at all in the land.
verses.30:9: Now I have been turned into their song, and I have been made a proverb to them.
verses.30:10: They abhor me, and they flee far from me, and they do not fear to spit on my face.
verses.30:11: For He has opened His quiver and afflicted me, and He has placed a bridle in my mouth.
verses.30:12: At the right hand of the east my calamities rose up at once; they overturned my feet and overwhelmed them as with waves by their paths.
verses.30:13: They broke up my roads; they lay in wait for me and prevailed, and there was no one to bring help.
verses.30:14: As with a broken wall and an open gate, they rushed upon me, and rolled down to my miseries.
verses.30:15: I have been reduced to nothing; like the wind You have carried away my desire, and like a cloud my safety has passed by.
verses.30:16: But now my soul withers within myself, and days of affliction possess me.
verses.30:17: At night my bone is pierced with pains, and those who eat me do not sleep.
verses.30:18: In their multitude my garment is consumed, and like the collar of a tunic they have bound me around.
verses.30:19: I have been compared to mud, and I have been made like cinders and ashes.
verses.30:20: I cry out to You, and You do not hear me; I stand, and You do not look at me.
verses.30:21: You have changed into a cruel one toward me, and in the hardness of Your hand You oppose me.
verses.30:22: You have lifted me up, and as if placing me upon the wind, You have dashed me down violently.
verses.30:23: I know that You will hand me over to death, where a house is appointed for every living being.
verses.30:24: Nevertheless, You do not put forth Your hand for their destruction, and if they fall down, You Yourself will save them.
verses.30:25: Once I wept over the one who was afflicted, and my soul had compassion on the poor.
verses.30:26: I expected good things, and evil things came to me; I waited for light, and darkness burst forth.
verses.30:27: My inward parts have boiled up without any rest; days of affliction have overtaken me.
verses.30:28: I went about mourning, without fury; rising up, I cried out in the crowd.
verses.30:29: I have been a brother of dragons, and a companion of ostriches.
verses.30:30: My skin has turned black upon me, and my bones have dried up from the scorching heat.
verses.30:31: My lyre has been turned into mourning, and my flute into the voice of those who weep.
verses.31:1: I have made a covenant with my eyes, so that I would not even think about a virgin.
verses.31:2: For what portion would God from above have in me, and what inheritance the Almighty from on high?
verses.31:3: Is there not destruction for the wicked man, and estrangement for those who work injustice?
verses.31:4: Does He Himself not consider my ways, and count all my steps?
verses.31:5: If I have walked in vanity, and my foot has hurried in deceit,
verses.31:6: let Him weigh me on a just scale, and let God know my integrity.
verses.31:7: If my step has turned aside from the way, and if my heart has followed my eyes, and if a stain has clung to my hands,
verses.31:8: let me sow, and let another eat, and let my offspring be uprooted.
verses.31:9: If my heart has been deceived over a woman, and if I have lain in wait at my friend's door,
verses.31:10: let my wife be another's prostitute, and let others bow down over her.
verses.31:11: For this is a heinous crime, and the greatest iniquity.
verses.31:12: It is a fire devouring even to destruction, and uprooting all produce.
verses.31:13: If I have scorned to submit to judgment with my male servant and my female servant, when they contended against me,
verses.31:14: for what will I do when God rises to judge? And when He inquires, what will I answer Him?
verses.31:15: Did not He who also fashioned him make me in the womb, and did not One and the same form me in the womb?
verses.31:16: If I have denied to the poor what they wanted, and made the eyes of the widow wait;
verses.31:17: if I have eaten my morsel alone, and the orphan has not eaten from it
verses.31:18: (for from my infancy compassion grew with me, and from my mother's womb it came out with me);
verses.31:19: if I have despised one who was perishing because he had no clothing, and a poor man without a covering;
verses.31:20: if his sides have not blessed me, and he has been warmed by the fleeces of my sheep;
verses.31:21: if I have raised my hand against the orphan, even when I saw myself superior in the gate,
verses.31:22: let my shoulder fall away from its joint, and let my arm be shattered along with its bones.
verses.31:23: For always, like waves swelling over me, I feared God, and I could not bear His weight.
verses.31:24: If I have considered gold my strength, and said to fine gold, 'My confidence';
verses.31:25: if I have rejoiced over my many riches, and because my hand has found very much;
verses.31:26: if I have seen the sun when it shone, and the moon moving brightly,
verses.31:27: and my heart has rejoiced in secret, and I have kissed my hand with my mouth,
verses.31:28: which is the greatest iniquity, and a denial against God Most High.
verses.31:29: If I have been glad at the ruin of the one who hated me, and exulted that evil had found him,
verses.31:30: for I have not given my throat to sin, so that by cursing I would demand his life.
verses.31:31: If the men of my tent have not said, 'Who will give some of his flesh, so that we may be satisfied?'
verses.31:32: The stranger did not stay outside; my door stood open to the traveler.
verses.31:33: If I have hidden my sin like a man, and concealed my iniquity in my bosom;
verses.31:34: if I have been terrified at a very great multitude, and the contempt of relatives has frightened me, and I have not rather kept silent, nor gone out the door.
verses.31:35: Who will grant me a hearer, so that the Almighty may hear my desire, and that He Himself who judges may write a book,
verses.31:36: that I may carry it on my shoulder, and place it around myself like a crown?
verses.31:37: At each of my steps I will declare it, and as to a prince I will offer it.
verses.31:38: If my land cries out against me, and with it its furrows weep,
verses.31:39: if I have eaten its fruits without money, and I have afflicted the soul of its farmers,
verses.31:40: instead of wheat let the thistle spring up for me, and instead of barley the thorn." The words of Job are finished.
verses.32:1: Now these three men stopped answering Job, because he seemed righteous to himself.
verses.32:2: And Elihu, son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, became angry and indignant; he was angry against Job because he said that he was righteous before God.
verses.32:3: Moreover, he was indignant against his friends because they had not found a reasonable answer, but had merely condemned Job.
verses.32:4: Therefore, Elihu waited for Job while he was speaking, because those who were speaking were older.
verses.32:5: But when he saw that the three had not been able to answer, he became intensely angry.
verses.32:6: And Elihu, son of Barachel the Buzite, answered and said, "I am younger in years, while you are older; for that reason, with my head bowed, I was afraid to declare my opinion to you.
verses.32:7: For I was hoping that a more advanced age would speak, and that a multitude of years would teach wisdom.
verses.32:8: But, as I see, there is a spirit in human beings, and the inspiration of the Almighty gives understanding.
verses.32:9: The long-lived are not the wise, nor do the elderly understand judgment.
verses.32:10: Therefore I will say, 'Listen to me; I too will show you my wisdom.'
